sections.label: The opening
sections.line: An afternoon's turns, from a £50 site on Kickstarter to a configured Android tablet and a Raspberry Pi.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Where it started, where it ended, eleven turns, what held, and the plan in the next piece.

sections.label: Where the afternoon started
sections.line: The morning's pieces were out; the next question was the launch.

sections.label: 1. Why not Kickstarter?
sections.line: Kickstarter's rules on services and AI, and Portugal not a creator country.

sections.label: 2. Indiegogo, PPL and Product Hunt
sections.line: Indiegogo all-or-nothing, PPL second, Product Hunt; one campaign, not three.

sections.label: 3. Patreon
sections.line: Patreon sells one-offs but is built for ongoing support: the second act.

sections.label: 4. Countries as stretch goals
sections.line: Bring sovereign websites to the world, one country at a time.

sections.label: 5. The UK is home ground
sections.line: The UK is home ground, in the base goal; Portugal the first stretch goal.

sections.label: 6. Places, not languages
sections.line: Every language from day one, so stretch goals are places; revealed as you go; paid at the end.

sections.label: 7. A hardware appliance
sections.line: A tablet configured with everything, which brings Kickstarter back.

sections.label: 8. iPad or Android
sections.line: Android first; TestFlight is not a shop; iOS a stretch goal; a website is an application.

sections.label: 9. Cost plus 50%, then a simpler promise
sections.line: Cost plus 50% replaced by what we spend: about £250 of a £500 pledge, £500 of £1,000.

sections.label: 10. A £50 supporter, and no T-shirt
sections.line: A £50 supporter tier for the site alone, add-ons above, and no T-shirt.

sections.label: 11. A Raspberry Pi too
sections.line: A Raspberry Pi too: the same deploy, to a box at home.

sections.label: What held throughout
sections.line: One campaign, value first, the UK first, open source, launching alone.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A record of thinking; rules as read that day; nothing submitted.
